channel.title: Family Dinner Plan
channel.description: A few minutes every Saturday walking through the coming week's family dinners: what's cooking each night and one quick tip per meal. This podcast uses AI-generated voices; scripts are written by AI.

item.title: Week of October 31, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: Okay, the thing that's going to make or break this week happens tonight, and it's not even a dinner — it's a spatchcock.
BUB: A what?
BENDY: Spatchcock. Tomorrow's chicken goes on the Traeger whole, but I'm cutting the backbone out tonight so it lays flat. Flat chicken cooks evenly — skin gets crackly all over instead of rubbery on one side.
BUB: So what do I actually do today, before the week starts?
BENDY: First, pull the stew meat for Thursday's stroganoff out of the freezer, it needs the full day to thaw in the fridge. Second, rice up a head of cauliflower — you'll need it twice this week, Monday and Wednesday, so do a double batch now and bag half.
BUB: And the chicken?
BENDY: Backbone out tonight, chicken dries uncovered in the fridge overnight. Dry skin plus hot grill equals crackle. Wet skin equals steam, and steam equals sad rubbery skin.
BUB: Noted. Sad rubbery skin, avoid at all costs.
BENDY: Sunday it's the Traeger Peruvian Whole Roasted Chicken with Green Sauce and Fall Vegetables — I'm tossing delicata squash wedges in with the veg, skin stays on, no peeling.
BUB: Wait, you can eat the skin on that squash?
BENDY: Thin skin, roasts tender. Try it before you decide.
BENDY: Monday's the Slow Cooker Honey Sesame Chicken. Thighs go in frozen, straight from the freezer bag, no thawing required.
BUB: Isn't that supposed to be bad, cooking stuff frozen?
BENDY: Not in a slow cooker on low for six-plus hours — it comes up to temp slow and even. The trick is don't thicken the sauce till the last thirty minutes, or the cornstarch breaks down and goes thin and weird.
BENDY: Tuesday, hamburger steaks. Southern Style Hamburger Steak with Onion Mushroom Gravy and Roasted Green Beans. Mushrooms get added after the onions are already soft and golden.
BUB: Why not all together?
BENDY: Mushrooms dump water when they hit the pan. Add them early with raw onions and everything just steams instead of browning.
BENDY: Wednesday — Honey Orange Glazed Pork Stir Fry with Cauliflower Rice. That's where the second bag of riced cauliflower pays off. Pork goes in hot oil in one layer, don't crowd the pan.
BUB: Or?
BENDY: Crowd it, it steams, you get gray pork instead of a sear with color on it.
BENDY: Thursday, the stroganoff you thawed tonight — Slow Cooker Beef Stroganoff with Zucchini Noodles. Zoodles go in raw at the very end, like the last five minutes, just to warm through.
BUB: Let me guess. Or they turn to mush.
BENDY: You're learning. Exactly that.
BENDY: Friday's easy — Whole30 Sonoma Chicken Salad Lettuce Wraps. Use the extra roasted chicken from Sunday if there's any left, shred it cold straight from the fridge.
BUB: So Sunday's chicken basically pays us back twice.
BENDY: That's the whole plan. Saturday's takeout, no excuses.
BUB: And tonight — backbone out, cauliflower riced, meat out of the freezer.
BENDY: Say it with me: dry skin, big crackle.
BUB: Dry skin, big crackle. Got it.

item.title: Week of October 24, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: One bird on the Traeger tomorrow, and that same bird turns into Friday dinner.
BUB: The exact same chicken? Six days later?
BENDY: Not six. Sunday it's dinner, Friday the picked-off meat goes into lettuce wraps. In between it sits in the fridge being useful.
BUB: So the chicken is the main character.
BENDY: The chicken is basically the whole cast. Which is why today matters.
BENDY: Here's the Saturday list. Whole chicken out of the freezer right now, into the fridge, breast up on a sheet pan. A four-pounder needs a full day and then some.
BUB: What if it's still frozen in the middle?
BENDY: Then the skin burns before the thighs are done. That's the whole reason we're doing it today.
BENDY: Tonight, salt it. Teaspoon of kosher salt per pound, up under the breast skin too, then leave it uncovered in the fridge. Dry skin crisps. Wet skin steams.
BENDY: Also tonight: the cashew sauce. Coconut aminos, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, a little chili. It sits better overnight anyway.
BUB: Can I smash the cashews?
BENDY: You can smash the cashews. Put them in a bag, use the bottom of a pan, leave some big pieces.
BENDY: At the store: two heads of cauliflower, three heads of butter lettuce, a delicata squash, a butternut, a couple sweet potatoes, Brussels sprouts, green chiles, and ground beef for Tuesday.
BENDY: Rice both cauliflowers today while the processor's already dirty. Two bags, one for Wednesday, one spare. And pull the chili beef down to the fridge tomorrow night.
BENDY: Sunday is Traeger Whole Roasted Chicken with Fall Vegetables. Smoke at 225 for an hour, then crank to 375 to finish. One temperature the whole way and you get rubbery skin.
BUB: What temperature is it done?
BENDY: 165 in the thigh, not the breast. The breast lies.
BENDY: Monday, Cashew Chicken Lettuce Wraps. Cook the chicken in two batches in a hot pan. Crowd it and it dumps water and turns gray.
BUB: It got messy last time.
BENDY: It will again. Double up the lettuce leaves.

item.title: Week of October 17, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: The chicken you rub tonight shows up twice this week. Sunday it's hot off the Traeger, Thursday it's cold, sliced thin, and folded into lettuce wraps.
BUB: Same chicken? Two dinners?
BENDY: Same chicken, two dinners. Which is why we're cooking eight thighs Sunday instead of four.
BUB: What do we do today?
BENDY: Three things. Stew meat and ground chicken out of the freezer and into the fridge, on a plate, bottom shelf. They'll be thawed by the time we need them.
BUB: And the pork?
BENDY: Pork goes in Monday night. Second thing: green goddess tonight. Blitz the herbs, garlic, lemon and yogurt, then split it. Half goes on the thighs in a bag right now. Half stays in the fridge, untouched, for Thursday's dressing.
BUB: Why not just use it all?
BENDY: Because cooked herbs go brown and bitter. The raw half is the one that tastes like a garden.
BENDY: Third thing, the store. Two heads of cauliflower, one for ricing, one broken into florets for the stew. A butternut squash, Brussels sprouts, broccoli, mushrooms. And two heads of butter lettuce plus romaine, because we're eating leaves twice.
BUB: That's a lot of leaves.
BENDY: Wash and dry them today and stack them in a towel. Soggy lettuce tears.
BENDY: Sunday, Traeger Green Goddess Chicken Thighs with Roasted Fall Vegetables. Smoke at 225 for half an hour, then up to 375 to finish. Pull them at 175, not 165.
BUB: Isn't 165 the safe number?
BENDY: Safe, yes. But thigh meat has connective tissue that needs those extra ten degrees to go soft. At 165 it's rubbery.
BENDY: Squash and sprouts go on a sheet pan underneath, cut side down. They get the drippings.
BENDY: Monday, Slow Cooker Beef Stew with Cauliflower and Mushrooms. Brown the beef in batches first, and sear the mushrooms dry in a hot pan before they go in.
BUB: Can't I just dump it?
BENDY: You can, and it'll taste gray. Also hold the cauliflower until the last 45 minutes or it dissolves into the broth.

item.title: Week of October 10, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: One pork shoulder, two completely different dinners. Monday it's lemongrass and lime. Wednesday it's smoke and barbecue sauce. Same cut, nobody notices.
BUB: Wait, is it the same pork? Like, the actual same meat?
BENDY: Same cut, two batches. Which brings me to today, because today is the whole trick.
BUB: Here it comes.
BENDY: Freezer, right now. Whole chicken for tomorrow, both pork shoulders, and the chicken thighs for Thursday. Fridge, not counter. The pork needs two full days.
BUB: Two days for frozen pork?
BENDY: A shoulder is dense. Half-thawed means it cooks uneven and the middle stays tough. Tonight, dry-brine the chicken — salt it all over, uncovered in the fridge, and leave it. That's how the skin gets crisp instead of rubbery.
BUB: Naked chicken in the fridge all night.
BENDY: Dry skin, Bub. Dry skin is the whole glaze plan. Also tonight: blend the lemongrass marinade so Monday is just dump and walk away. And at the store, grab two big cauliflower heads, delicata squash, a couple sweet potatoes, broccoli, mushrooms, and oranges.
BUB: Two cauliflowers?
BENDY: One gets riced Thursday, one gets roasted. If you rice it today it goes damp and smells like a gym bag by Thursday.
BENDY: Sunday: Traeger Citrus Maple Glazed Chicken with Roasted Fall Vegetables. Chicken goes on around 325, and the glaze waits until the last twenty minutes.
BUB: Why not glaze it the whole time?
BENDY: Maple is sugar. Sugar over an hour of smoke turns bitter and black. Twenty minutes gets you that sticky, shiny orange-brown instead. Delicata and sweet potatoes on a separate pan — the squash skin is edible, so don't peel it.
BUB: That's my favorite part. It gets chewy.
BENDY: Monday: Slow Cooker Lemongrass Pork Bowls. Low for eight hours, and don't drown it. A quarter

item.title: Week of October 03, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: One batch of lemon basil pesto on Sunday afternoon is going to carry us all the way to Wednesday.
BUB: The same sauce twice?
BENDY: Three times, technically. Marinade Sunday, dipping sauce Sunday, and then it's the whole point of Wednesday's dinner.
BUB: Sneaky.
BENDY: Efficient. So here's today, in the car, before we even get home. Pull three packs of chicken breasts out of the freezer and the flank steak too. They go in the fridge, not on the counter.
BUB: Why not the counter?
BENDY: Because the outside thaws way faster than the middle and sits warm for hours. Fridge takes a day and a half and it's fine.
BENDY: Tonight I'm making a double batch of pesto. Basil, garlic, parm, lemon zest and juice, olive oil. Half goes in a bag with the chicken for Sunday, half stays sealed in a jar with a thin film of oil on top so it doesn't go brown.
BUB: What about the squash?
BENDY: Good. Butternut and Brussels sprouts today, and I'll peel and cube the squash tonight so Sunday is just oil, salt, sheet pan. Also two heads of cauliflower, because we're ricing both at once in the food processor and splitting it for Tuesday and Thursday.
BUB: Both at once?
BENDY: I am not pulling that processor out twice. Pulse it, don't run it, or you get cauliflower mush.
BENDY: Sunday is Lemon Pesto Grilled Chicken with Roasted Butternut Squash and Brussels Sprouts. Traeger at 425, chicken comes off at 160 and rests five minutes.
BUB: Not 165?
BENDY: It climbs while it rests. Pull at 165 and you've got sawdust. The reserved pesto goes on after it rests, never before the grill, or the basil scorches.
BENDY: Monday, 20 Minute Cashew Chicken Lettuce Wraps. Sear the chicken in two batches in a hot pan.
BUB: Why two?
BENDY: Crowd the pan and the chicken steams in its own juice. No browning, no flavor. Toast the cashews dry for two minutes first.
BENDY: Tuesday, Crockpot Chicken Tikka Masala with Cauliflower Rice. Bloom the garam masala and ginger in oil for thirty seconds before it goes in the crock.
BUB: Thirty seconds does something?
BENDY: It wakes the spices up. Skip it and eight hours later it still tastes dusty. Cream goes in the last ten minutes or it splits.
BENDY: Wednesday, Pesto Basil Chicken and Zoodles. Salt the zoodles, let them sit ten minutes, squeeze them in a towel.
BUB: That sounds like a lot of water.
BENDY: It's a shocking amount. Skip it and you're eating pesto soup. Sauce goes on off the heat.
BENDY: Thursday, Mongolian Beef with Broccoli and Cauliflower Rice. Slice the flank steak thin against the grain while it's still half frozen.
BUB: Against the grain means across the lines?
BENDY: Across the lines. With them and it's chewy no matter how long you cook it.
BENDY: Friday, Easy Orange Pork Stir Fry. Zest the oranges before you juice them, and mix the cornstarch into cold sauce, not hot pan.
BUB: Or lumps.
BENDY: Or lumps. Saturday is takeout, and nobody touches the stove.
BENDY: And if you only do one thing today, make the pesto.

item.title: Week of September 26, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: Tuesday's beef roast does double duty this week. We eat it with mushrooms and balsamic, then Wednesday it goes inside a butternut squash with enchilada sauce.
BUB: Inside the squash? Like the squash is the tortilla?
BENDY: The squash is the bowl. Roasted till the edges go sweet and a little sticky.
BUB: Okay. I'm listening.
BENDY: Today, though. Today is the easy day, and I want to use it. Pull the chuck roast and the ground turkey out of the freezer and into the fridge right now. A three-pound roast needs a full day and a half to thaw, and a half-frozen roast in the slow cooker means gray meat that never gets tender.
BUB: What about tonight?
BENDY: Tonight I rub the chicken. Salt, pepper, thyme, garlic, all over and under the skin, then it sits uncovered in the fridge. That dry overnight sit is what gets the skin crisp on the Traeger instead of rubbery.
BUB: And shopping?
BENDY: A head of cauliflower for Monday, a butternut for Wednesday, two apples for Friday, cucumbers and tomatoes and a lemon for Thursday. If I have twenty minutes tonight, I rice half the cauliflower and make the tzatziki. Tzatziki is better on day two anyway, once the garlic settles down.
BENDY: Sunday is Traeger French Chicken with Creamy Dijon Sauce. Smoke at 225 for forty minutes, then crank to 400 to finish. Pull it at 165 in the thigh.
BUB: Why two temperatures?
BENDY: Low gets smoke in, high gets the skin tight. One temperature gives you one or the other. And the Dijon sauce goes together in the pan drippings after, off the heat, or the cream splits.
BENDY: Monday, Slow Cooker Zuppa Toscana with Cauliflower. Brown the sausage first, hard, in a skillet. Raw sausage dumped in the crock just poaches and the broth tastes flat.
BUB: Does the cauliflower get mushy?
BENDY: Riced cauliflower goes in the last thirty minutes. Any earlier and it dissolves.
BENDY: Tuesday, Slow Cooker Balsamic Beef Roast with Mushrooms. Sear all six sides, then eight hours on low. Not high. High tightens the muscle before the collagen has time to melt.
BUB: Eight hours is a whole school day.
BENDY: That's the point. Wednesday, Leftover Beef Enchilada Stuffed Butternut Squash. Roast the halves cut side down at 400 for forty-five minutes first, then flip, fill, and broil the cheese. Fill it raw and you get crunchy squash under hot beef.
BENDY: Thursday, Greek Turkey Meatball Bowls. Don't pack the meatballs. Roll them loose, barely holding, bake at 400 for eighteen minutes. Squeezed meatballs come out springy and dry.
BUB: Extra tzatziki on mine.
BENDY: Friday, Sausage Apple And Goat Cheese Frittata. Cook the apples down until they give up their water. Wet apples make a soggy middle that never sets.
BUB: Saturday?
BENDY: Takeout, and nobody cooks. Now go move that roast to the fridge before I forget I asked.

item.title: Week of September 19, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: Huli means turn. That's the whole trick — you turn the chicken and mop it with sauce, turn and mop, until the outside goes sticky and almost lacquered.
BUB: How many times?
BENDY: Four or five over about forty minutes. Every time you open the Traeger you're painting on another layer.
BUB: So it's like a chicken with paint.
BENDY: A chicken with six coats of paint. Okay — today. Pull the chicken thighs for tomorrow out of the freezer now, into the fridge, and the pork shoulder for Tuesday too.
BUB: Both?
BENDY: Both. A shoulder that's still icy in the middle takes forever to break down. While those thaw, make the huli huli sauce tonight — soy, pineapple juice, brown sugar, ginger, garlic, rice vinegar. Simmer it five minutes so it thickens slightly.
BUB: Why tonight?
BENDY: Because half of it becomes the marinade and the thighs sit in it overnight. Reserve the other half in a jar and don't let it touch raw chicken — that's your mopping sauce.
BENDY: Then: two delicata squash, a big head of broccoli, Brussels sprouts, a head of cauliflower. Cut the cauliflower into florets today and bag it. Mix the meatballs tonight too and roll them, on a sheet pan in the fridge.
BUB: Rolling meatballs is the best part.
BENDY: It's yours. Sunday — Traeger at 375, thighs skin side up, and the delicata gets cut in half-moons, seeds scooped, skin left on.
BUB: You don't peel it?
BENDY: You don't have to. The skin on delicata goes tender. Broccoli goes in the last twelve minutes or it turns gray and sad.
BENDY: Monday, the tomatoes. Get the pan hot and leave them alone until they split and leak. If you stir too early they just roll around staying whole and you get no sauce.
BUB: And the zucchini noodles?
BENDY: Thirty seconds in the pan, max. Longer than that and they water out and it's soup.
BUB: Noodle soup, though.
BENDY: Not the good kind. Tuesday, carnitas — eight hours on low with orange, lime, garlic, cumin. Then shred it and run it under the broiler four minutes on a sheet pan.
BUB: Why?
BENDY: Because slow cooker pork is tender but it's soft all the way through. The broiler gives you crispy edges. That's the part people fight over. Pineapple pico with red onion and cilantro, and lettuce cups instead of tortillas.
BENDY: Wednesday, ginger orange chicken with the sprouts. Sprouts cut side down, and give the chicken its own corner of the pan.
BUB: Crowded pan means steamed, not roasted.
BENDY: Look at you. Thursday, sausage and peppers — brown the sausage coins first and pull them out before the peppers go in. Otherwise they sit in pepper steam and never get color. Roasted cauliflower alongside, 425 until the tips go dark.
BENDY: And Wednesday, cook two extra chicken breasts. Friday is the remix — everything chopped fine and rolled into cabbage leaves.
BUB: Leftovers in disguise.
BENDY: Leftovers with a new job. Saturday, takeout, and nobody touches the stove.

item.title: Week of September 12, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: Thursday night I'm making honey sesame chicken, and Friday I'm chopping the leftovers into a salad with the same sauce as the dressing. One sauce, two dinners, zero complaining.
BUB: Cold chicken on lettuce?
BENDY: Warm chicken, cold lettuce. Trust me Friday.
BUB: I'm writing this down so I can hold you to it.
BENDY: Fair. Now, today, while we're out. Pull the pork tenderloin and the stir-fry beef into the fridge to thaw overnight. Frozen in the middle Sunday means a gray, tough edge by the time the center catches up.
BUB: What about the chicken?
BENDY: Two packs of chicken thighs, one for Monday's slow cooker soup, one for Thursday. Those can thaw Sunday and Wednesday.
BUB: And the cauliflower?
BENDY: Three heads, or bagged riced if the store has it. We need rice for Monday and Thursday, plus zucchini for Tuesday's noodles. I'll spiralize those tonight and salt them lightly on a towel in the fridge.
BUB: Why salt them?
BENDY: Zucchini is mostly water. Salt pulls it out now so Tuesday's stir-fry isn't soup.
BENDY: Tonight I'm also mixing the herb rub, rosemary, thyme, garlic, salt, brown sugar, and rubbing the pork. It sits in the fridge overnight and the salt gets all the way in.
BENDY: Sunday is Traeger Herb-Rubbed Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Brussels Sprouts & Apples. Traeger at 375, pork comes off at 140 internal and rests ten minutes. Cut it early and all that juice runs onto the board instead of staying in the meat.
BUB: Ten whole minutes?
BENDY: Ten. That's when the sprouts and apple wedges finish, cut side down, so the sprouts get dark and the apples go jammy.
BENDY: Monday, Creamy Chicken & Cauliflower Rice Soup in the slow cooker. Low six hours, but the riced cauliflower goes in the last thirty minutes. All day in there and it dissolves into paste.
BUB: So it's a late add.
BENDY: Late add. Same with the cream, off the heat, or it splits and looks curdled.
BENDY: Tuesday, Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry with Zucchini Noodles. Hot pan, beef in one layer, don't stir for ninety seconds. Crowd it and it steams instead of browning, and you lose the whole point.
BUB: Is that why it smells different when it works?
BENDY: Exactly why. Brown smells sweet. Steamed smells like nothing.
BENDY: Wednesday, Sausage, White Bean & Kale Soup. Brown the sausage first and cook the mushrooms in that fat until they squeak and shrink. Skip it and the broth tastes thin, like beans in water.
BUB: Kale last?
BENDY: Kale last, five minutes, still a little green.
BENDY: Thursday, Slow Cooker Honey Sesame Chicken with Cauliflower Rice. Thighs, not breasts, and thicken the sauce on the stove at the end. Straight from the crock it's watery and slides off the rice.
